summary: Sonam Thakchoe specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed a doctorate at the University of Tasmania (1999–2002) mentored by Jay L. Garfield and Jeff Malpas, later becoming a Senior Philosophy Lecturer there in 2003.

Sonam Tsering works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Gray Tuttle, Janet Gyatso, Leonard van der Kuijp, and several traditional teachers. As of 2026, he is Senior Lecturer in Tibetan and Director of the Tibetan Language Program at Columbia University.
Sondra L. Hausner is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Attested in 2026, she serves as Professor of Anthropology of Religion at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford.

Songeun Choe specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Choe completed an MA under the supervision of Myung-dae Moon and doctoral studies supervised by Kiyohiko Munakata (attested 1991).

Sonika Gupta works in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She earned an M.A. from Jawaharlal Nehru University (1993–1997) and became a Professor at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras in 2025.

Sonja Arntzen is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. She earned her BA (1962–1966) and PhD (1970–1979) at the University of British Columbia, completing her doctorate under Leon Hurvitz, and also studied under Seizan Yanagida and Sojo Hirano.

Sonja Glauch is a scholar of linguistics. She completed her Magisterexamen, Promotion, and Habilitation at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, where she became Akademische Oberrätin in 2007, alongside posts at Heidelberg, Vienna, and Munich.

Sonya S. Lee specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under Hung Wu, taught at Swarthmore College (2003–2004), and held posts at the University of Southern California and Stanford University.

Soonil Hwang is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed an MA at Dongguk University under Seung-won Seo and a DPhil at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich, later becoming a professor at Dongguk University in 2004.

Soorakkulame Pemaratana is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at the National University of Singapore under Saranindranath Tagore. In 2026, he is attested as a Visiting Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

Sophus Bugge was a Norwegian scholar of linguistics. He studied at the University of Oslo, Copenhagen, and Berlin under Albrecht Weber and Niels Ludvig Westergaard, later serving as stipendiat (1860–1864) and lektor (1866) at the University of Oslo.
Soshu Nishioka is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Shitennoji University, attested in 2000 and 2015.

Soshuku Shibatani specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Waseda University and Koyasan University (master's and doctorate), he has held posts as a researcher at Koyasan University (attested 2015, 2026) and lecturer at Sonoda Women's University.

Sotan Oka was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bokusan Nishiari, Teizo Shiratori, and Fusho Nagano. He served as professor and dean (1899) and president (1918) at Komazawa University, and founded Antai-ji in 1921.

Soumyajit Sen is an Indology scholar who earned a BA from Ramakrishna Mission Vidyamandira and a Ph.D. from Jadavpur University (2016–2022). He became an Assistant Professor at Cooch Behar Panchanan Barma University in 2016.

Soyen Shaku was a Buddhist studies scholar and philosopher. He studied at Keio University and under teachers including Ekkei Shuken and Kōsen Imakita, later serving as Zen master at Engaku-ji (1892) and president of Hanazono University (1914–1917).
Spiridon Dmitrievič Èl’manovič was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University from 1865 to 1869 and served as director of Kholm Gymnasium in 1896.

Sravana Borkataky-Varma is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Delhi and Rice University (PhD 2012–2018). Her academic positions include appointments at Rice, Harvard, UNC Wilmington, and the University of Houston.

Sravani Kanamarlapudi is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. She studied at the University of Washington (2019) under Richard G. Salomon and is attested as a PhD student at the University of Texas at Austin in 2026.

Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Visva-Bharati, Andhra University, and the University of Marburg (PhD ~1960–1966), later serving as a professor at Aligarh Muslim University (~1977–1997).
